issues.claim: R6-02's *beneath* (base l. 2640–2646) rules that a `vault` span whose under-deck strip meets a wall's band or wall strip "is read `open` by every reader of its `use` while that band or strip lies there … its record unchanged". V09 §4.20.6 (2) (l. 3196–3199) applies it to the span's panel, its raised way's panel, the badge and the why card ("A wall runs under this arch"). V10's raised-way read row (l. 1686) gives "each span's use with its reason … from the base's span record", so the clerk tells the arch under T110-2 (3)'s c14 ring as a vault (and names a vault V04 never lays) while the card on the same span says open. Two units, two outcomes; R6-02's sweep searched V10 only for crossing-rule words. Sibling of VAL-R6-03 (§11.1's GeoJSON row), a different unit.
issues.required_change: 1. V10 l. 1686, the raised-way row's last cell: "each span's use with its reason (`open` by way, water, flood, tall, low, slope or land; `vault`; `user`) from the base's span record" → "each span's use with its reason (`open` by way, water, flood, tall, low, slope or land; `vault`; `user`) from the base's span record — but a span whose under-deck strip a wall's band or wall strip meets is told `open` while that band or strip lies there, with "a wall runs under this arch", whatever its recorded `use`, and no arch vault named in it (§2.7's crossing table, *beneath*; V09 §4.20.6 (2))". 2. T-V10-41 adds: "on T110-2 (3)'s c14 fixture with a `vault` span of its S4 viaduct under stage 2's ring, the clerk's read of the viaduct tells that span `open` with "a wall runs under this arch", as its V09 panel and why card do, and after a hand `delete` of that run tells it `vault` with its arch vault".

issues.claim: The crossing table's row W3, "a regeneration re-deriving a ring under a held raised way" (base l. 2700), names T110-2 (6) as the test of its cells C3 (one span fallen), C4 (all fallen), C5 (a support cleared or toppled), C6 (a `vault` span breached) and C10–C13. T110-2 (6) (l. 18598–18607) regenerates only standing held raised ways. At generation every raised way is new, so a regeneration is the only time S3's and S5a's pull, S4's crossing rule, S10's band and V04's T2 vaults step meet fallen parts and must read a `ruined` stump as impassable, a `cleared` ring as open ground, the clear width between standing rings only, the run at its own top beneath a fallen span and no chamber in a breached span. T110-2 (7) runs V06's epoch cost field, T110-2 (4) the hand operator's local bend and T-V6-47 the epoch re-solve, so a generation-path build that reads every recorded support as standing passes every bar, and at Regenerate (keep) or New random of a town whose held aqueduct has lapsed it routes the ring round a cleared support or caps a run at a fallen soffit.
issues.required_change: §13.2's T110-2 (6), after "0 S5b or S5c way corridors over a support ring, ramp, stair or foot" (the clause's end, before "(7) parts going"), add: "; and (1)'s c15 fixture with its aqueduct locked after scripted `DeclineOp`s — a span over the band `ruined`, a support by the band `cleared` and a `vault` span over the trace breached — regenerated (keep), then given New random with its seed searched so that the new ring's boundary meets the `cleared` support's former ring and, on a second run, a `ruined` support's stump: the trace through the cleared ring as open ground and crossing the deck line clear of the stump as of a standing support, the band whole across each former footprint, the run at its own top beneath each fallen span, no arch vault in the breached span, each S4 route the regeneration re-solves crossing the deck under a span §4.3 admits with its clear width read between standing rings, every station, key, span and state of the aqueduct unchanged (§2.7's crossing table, W3·C3–C6)".

issues.claim: R6-03 step 2 leaves uncarried, with a late calamity, "a condition naming it" (§4.11 *The clock* (4) l. 8531; V08 §3.6 (3) l. 1874, §3.2 l. 1530, §3.6 (4) l. 1927–1928, §3.17 row l. 2702, T-V8-49 (g)). A SettlementForge condition names no calamity: `activeConditions[]` carries `id`, `archetype`, `label`, `severity`, `severityBand`, `status`, `triggeredAt.tick`, `triggeredAt.sourceEventType`, `duration` (V08 l. 665). The only link is V08 §3.16 (7) (d)'s week rule over carried calamities: "the carried calamity whose week equals its `triggeredAt.tick`, else … the latest carried calamity in the 52 weeks up to its `sinceWeek`". Builders differ: exact week only, (d)'s whole rule with the deferred calamity counted carried, or label matching. A `reconstruction` condition raised a week after the calamity, in a town with an earlier carried calamity within 52 weeks, is carried by the first build and by (d) linked to the earlier calamity, so its disaster look stands on the wrong districts (V08 §3.16 (7) (b); §10.2 (d)) until the next absorb past `W₀` re-links it, a silent wrong look; T-V8-49 (g)'s "condition naming it" fixture fits whichever reading its author takes.
issues.required_change: 1. V08 §3.16 (7) (d), after "with none it carries no calamity.", add: "A condition **names** a calamity when this link would give it that calamity were it carried — its `triggeredAt.tick` at the calamity's week, else the calamity the latest in the 52 weeks up to the condition's `sinceWeek`; so a late calamity an absorb leaves uncarried (§4.11 *The clock* (4); V08 §3.6 (3)) holds back each condition that names it, none of them carried meanwhile or linked to an earlier calamity." 2. V08 §3.6 (3): "nor a condition naming it" → "nor a condition naming it (V08 §3.16 (7) (d))". 3. END (pipeline), §4.11 *The clock* (4): "nor a condition naming it" → "nor a condition naming it (V08 §3.16 (7) (d))". 4. T-V8-49 (g) adds: "and on a copy whose binding carries an earlier calamity in the 52 weeks before the second absorb, and whose `reconstruction` condition's `triggeredAt.tick` falls the week after the late calamity's — that condition not carried by the second absorb (no disaster look on the earlier calamity's districts), and carried by the absorb past `W₀` with the calamity, its look on the late calamity's targets".

issues.claim: *beneath*'s *Where the line crosses* (base l. 2617–2635) says "a trace's line never crosses … an aqueduct's standing support", and a stretch laid by no pull or cost field (a hand `drawWall`, a moved trace vertex, a re-anchored stretch, VS3's palisade, V06 §3.7.6 (3)'s quay wall, `repairWall`'s new stretch) "is bent locally, between its nearest points clear of the raised way's under-deck strip … on either side: to cross an aqueduct under the nearest span". That bend is written only for a stretch that crosses the deck line. A hand wall drawn along beneath an aqueduct (between or through its piers), a stretch entering and leaving the under-deck strip on one side, or a stretch drawn or a vertex moved to end at a pier has no "either side" and no crossing to move, so no outcome. Builders differ: move it to the strip's edge, force a crossing under a span (crossing twice), refuse it, or run it through the piers against T-V6-47's bar "0 trace lines across … an aqueduct's standing support". Not in the canon's catalogue; the probe and adjudication-r6 never consider it (pulled and cost-field traces, and road decks, are defined). Distinct from VEW-r6-03 (a barrier anchor or weld vertex inside a strip): no anchor rule reaches a hand stretch run along beneath an aqueduct or ended at one of its piers.
issues.required_change: 1. §2.7's crossing table, *beneath*, *Where the line crosses*: after "…through a gate there (by hand a fate named in `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s line)." add: "A stretch of that group whose line meets an aqueduct's standing support without crossing its deck line there — one drawn along beneath it, one entering and leaving its under-deck strip on one side, one ending at a support — is bent the same way: its part inside the strip moved to the strip's edge on the side it entered from, between its nearest points clear of the strip, an end inside the strip moved to that edge (by hand a fate in `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s line); so no such stretch runs along within, or ends inside, an aqueduct's under-deck strip." 2. END (determinism), §7.1's `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` row, outcome: after "under an aqueduct's nearest span," add "a stretch along beneath an aqueduct or ending at one of its supports moved to the under-deck strip's edge,". 3. END (scope), T110-2 (4): after "each a fate in `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s line;" add "a hand `drawWall` drawn along beneath a standing aqueduct through two of its supports, and one ending at a support — each moved to the under-deck strip's edge, a fate in `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s line, every station, key and span unchanged;". (The adjudicator may instead refuse such a drawing with its nearest lawful alternative under §7.1's catch-all; the bar in 3 then asserts that refusal.)
